motifs.label: Arms and legs in an X
motifs.definition: Lying with arms and legs spread diagonally so the body forms an X, used as the working configuration — typically with diagonal lengthening, opposite arm-and-leg reaching or lifting, or rolling organized along the diagonals.

motifs.label: Bell hands
motifs.definition: A soft, responsive open-and-close organization of the hand (wrist droops, fingertips approach the thumb, then the hand "uncloses") in which changes through the fingers and palm participate in, or are coupled to, movement and breath elsewhere in the body. Moshe's late "bell hand" device; often described via a jellyfish image.

motifs.label: Circular breathing (orbit)
motifs.definition: The breath is directed around a closed internal loop — typically up the back/spine and down the front (or reversed), sometimes extended through the neck and head. Related to Daoist "microcosmic orbit" practice.

motifs.label: Clock (imagined dial)
motifs.definition: An imagined clock face or dial placed on, under, or against a body part — the pelvis, a heel or foot, a shoulder or shoulder blade, the head, the sit bones on a chair — with named hours or dial positions organizing the direction, pressure, or timing of movement. Covers the pelvic clock, the clock under the heel, shoulder/side clocks, chair clocks, and other clock transpositions.

motifs.label: Eyes/jaw engagement
motifs.definition: Deliberate engagement of the eyes, or of the jaw/mouth/tongue, as a worked component of the lesson — even if only in part of it. Typical forms: eye-head differentiation (eyes move opposite to or independently of the head), eyes leading or organizing a movement, tracking or gaze work, monocular exploration, jaw-neck differentiation, mouth/tongue exploration. Broader than most motifs by design; the role field grades how much of the lesson it occupies.

motifs.label: Hand holding foot
motifs.definition: One or both hands grasp and hold a foot (or the toes, or the ankle together with the foot) as a sustained constraint that links arm and leg — cradling the leg, foot-to-head configurations, rocking while holding the foot, holding the soles while lying on the back.

motifs.label: Pressure waves through the body
motifs.definition: Repeated gentle pushes or pulses — commonly through the heels, feet, pelvis, or head — sent so that a wave of motion travels through the skeleton and the body visibly rocks or undulates along its length. The propagation of the wave itself is an object of attention: the lesson develops, varies, or tracks where the wave travels and where it stops.

motifs.label: See-saw (reciprocal) breathing
motifs.definition: With the breath held (or across the breath cycle), air/volume is exchanged between chest and abdomen — expand one as the other empties, reciprocally. Moshe's "see-saw breathing" (ATM book lesson 4); some teachers call it reciprocal or paradoxical breathing.
